name: What is Virtual Host?
description:
The term Virtual Host refers to the practice of running more than one web site (such as company1.example.com and company2.example.com) on a single machine. Virtual hosts can be IP-based, meaning that you have a different IP address for every web site, orname-based, meaning that you have multiple names running on each IP address. The fact that they are running on the same physical server is not apparent to the end user.

To use name-based virtual hosting, you must designate the IP address (and possibly port) on the server that will be accepting requests for the hosts. This is configured using the NameVirtualHost directive. In the normal case where any and all IP addresses on the server should be used, you can use * as the argument to NameVirtualHost. If you're planning to use multiple ports (e.g. running SSL) you should add a Port to the argument, such as *:80

name: Install Apache
description:
We will install apache package

yum install httpd
while its installing please go and create a freedns account here.We will see how to use this account later.

name: Setup files  and directories
description:
Lets first create our content serving directories.
mkdir -p /var/www/site1/public_html
mkdir -p /var/www/site2/public_html
Now we will set appropriate permissions:
chown -R apache:apache /var/www
chmod 755 /var/www
Finall, we will added the html content for first site. Feel free to edit this file whatever you want.
cd /var/www/site1/public_html/
echo "Welcome to Site100" > index.html
Now add content for second site
cd /var/www/site2/public_html/
echo "Welcome to another Site200" > index.html
So far we installed apache package created directories and files which will be used by apache process.

name: Setup httpd.conf file
description:
Under RedHat/CentOS machines, apache config file located at /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf. On this file, we will add just 3 directives. They are:
VirtualHost *:80 * tells to listen to all ipaddress on port 80 on this machine.
DocumentRoot Where to serve the html files
Servername name assiciated with this ipaddress.
We will append following data to default config
/etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf open the file and paste these lines at the end.
NameVirtualHost *:80
<VirtualHost *:80>                
    DocumentRoot /var/www/site1/public_html 
    ServerName site100.chickenkiller.com      
</VirtualHost>                                                                  
<VirtualHost *:80>    
    DocumentRoot /var/www/site2/public_html
    ServerName site200.chickenkiller.com              
</VirtualHost>
Now start the apache process
/etc/init.d/httpd start

name: Map IPaddress to a subdomain
description:
In order to access our html content via domain. We need to map our ipaddress, you can fetch it from /root/ directory. Just do
sudo ls /root
52.69.127.66 tmp

Goto -> https://freedns.afraid.org/subdomain/
Click on 'Add a new subdomain'
Enter 'Subdomain:' and ipaddress.
New subdomain should be similar (except ipaddr) to
